summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic headaches, including both migraines and benign intracranial hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hypertension due to likely primary hyperaldosteronism, and other comorbidities was admitted for a 10-day history of refractory, severe right-sided headaches with nausea, photophobia, and phonophobia. She had recently had a lumbar puncture showing elevated opening pressure, with transient relief. Her propranolol had been reduced, which may have contributed to headache recurrence. During admission, her propranolol was increased back to 20 mg twice daily, acetazolamide was increased to 500 mg twice daily, and she received an IV valproate bolus with partial improvement. Enalapril was restarted for blood pressure control. She was evaluated by endocrinology for suspected hyperaldosteronism, with plans for outpatient testing. She improved symptomatically, remained neurologically non-focal without papilledema, and was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
